title: Toeplitz Matrix
statement: You are given an `m x n` grid of integers `matrix`. It is called Toeplitz when, along every diagonal that runs down and to the right (from a cell to the cell one row lower and one column further right), all the values are identical. Return `true` if `matrix` is Toeplitz and `false` if it is not.
notes:
## Intuition

Every diagonal is a chain of cells, each one step down and to the right of the previous. All values on a chain are equal exactly when every link matches, that is, when each cell equals its upper-left neighbour. So there is no need to gather diagonals at all: one pass that compares every cell with the cell diagonally above it decides the answer. (Grouping values by `row - col` in a map also works, at the cost of extra memory.)

## Approach

1. Visit every cell that has an upper-left neighbour: rows from `1` and columns from `1`.
2. If `matrix[row][col]` differs from `matrix[row - 1][col - 1]`, a diagonal holds two different values, so return `false`.
3. If no comparison fails, every diagonal is constant; return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`matrix = [[1,2,3,4],[5,1,2,3],[9,5,1,2]]`. Row 1 compares `1, 2, 3` with the row above shifted by one: `1, 2, 3`, all equal. Row 2 compares `5, 1, 2` with `5, 1, 2` from row 1, again all equal. No check fails, so the answer is `true`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m · n): each cell is compared at most once.
- Space: O(1): only two loop indices.

## Pitfalls

- Start both loops at `1`; cells in the first row or column have no upper-left neighbour and must not be read at index `-1`.
- Compare with the upper-left cell, not the upper-right one: the diagonals run down and to the right.
- A single row or a single column is always Toeplitz, since every diagonal has one cell.
- This pass only ever needs the previous row, which answers the follow-up about loading one row at a time.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rows`, `cols` | the grid's height and width |
| `row` | current row, starting from the second |
| `col` | current column, starting from the second |
| `matrix[row - 1][col - 1]` | the upper-left neighbour on the same diagonal |

narration.2: Read the number of rows, m.
narration.3: Read the number of columns, n.
narration.4: Walk every row except the first, since the first row has nothing above it.
narration.5: Walk every column except the first, so each cell has an upper-left neighbour.
narration.6: Two neighbouring cells on one diagonal must hold the same value.
narration.7: They differ, so this diagonal is not constant and the matrix is not Toeplitz.
narration.11: Every cell matched its upper-left neighbour, so every diagonal is constant.
